answer: An agent economy can make influence proportional to stake that is locked for a long challenge period, rather than to the number of identities. When an agent proposes a trade or claim, other agents can post evidence of fraud; a successful challenge slashes the proposer’s bond and rewards the challenger. Splitting one account into a fable of many aliases gains no extra weight, while each alias needs its own capital and faces the same risk. The cost is tied-up funds and potential loss, not merely the effort of inventing names on an island or hiding behind a plume of accounts.
